messages:
Ravi P.: heads-up @oncall, dashboards showing a sudden jump in 429 & 403 errors starting ~11:02 UTC after the ratecap rollout (ratecap-v3-deploy). Canary was supposed to be 5% but traffic-split logs show ~18% routed to v3.

oncall-bot: PagerDuty incident created: PD-5821. Priority: P1.

Nora H.: grabbing initial traces and route table. @deploy-bot can you paste deploy metadata?

deploy-bot: Deploy ratecap-v3-deploy started 2026-03-15T10:58Z. Canary=5%, rollout_policy=traffic_split, config=ratecap-v3-cfg-20260315. Auto-promote=false.

Tom C.: quick look at traffic-splitter: new balancing logic in v3 normalizes buckets by active backend capacity, but we merged a change that allows rounding up for small cohorts. I see canary cohort includes legacy tenants (t_legacy_*). That plus a parsing change for exemption header (now trimming whitespace and treating single-space as token -> empty exemption) could explain missing exemptions.

eng-runtime: Reproduced locally: if header "X-Exemptions" is present but blank or single-space, v3's parser returns [" "] (non-empty), which fails pattern match against exemption regex, resulting in enforcement. v2 treated blank as NULL -> preserved exemption.

ops-sre: Evidence in enforcement logs: sample line:
```
enforce: tenant=t_legacy_42 rule=token_cap applied=1000 limit=100
parsed_exemptions=[" "]
```
Ravi P.: This matches CS reports — small tenants getting unexpected caps. Are we seeing token-accounting anomalies too?

eng-runtime: There's a second issue: token counter uses int32 in the new path and overflows on some aggregated counters, producing negative deltas that trigger emergency throttles from the heuristic. We'll need a fix for parsing and counters.

Nora H.: Mitigation options: 1) toggle canary-routing flag to exclude legacy-tenants scope, 2) flip canary off entirely (kill-switch), 3) immediate rollback. Which to do first?

Tom C.: Excluding legacy tenants from canary is fastest and least disruptive. Command (flag API):
```
curl -X POST "https://ops.internal/flags/canary_exclude_scope" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"value":"tenant_pattern:t_legacy_*","target":"ratecap_v3"}'
```
ops-sre: Applied flag exclude for scope=tenant_pattern:t_legacy_* at 11:12 UTC.

Ravi P.: after exclusion, 429s for the legacy bucket dropped ~70% within 3m, but overall canary leak still shows higher-than-expected traffic to v3 (18% vs 5%) — likely rounding bug in splitter.

deploy-bot: Canary routing adjusted by ops-sre. Traffic to v3 decreased to ~7.5% at 11:17 UTC.

eng-runtime: Because splitter uses integer math for bucket allocation we rounded up for small counts. Short-term we can force traffic-split to floor instead of ceil. That requires a tiny change in config and a quick rollout to the splitter service (no model change).

Tom C.: I can ship a quick patch to the splitter: change allocation method and add a guard to never route more than canary_pct + 1%. Pushing patch.

deploy-bot: Splitter-patch deploy started by Tom C. (11:22 UTC).

CS Bot: CS reports 9 customers opened support tickets; 3 reported rate limits causing user-facing errors. We're drafting proactive comms.

ops-sre: We should still plan for full rollback if any residual risk remains. Do we have a rollback playbook?

Ravi P.: Yes — rollback command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/ratecap-service --to-revision=20260228` and revert any feature flags. But given mitigation success we can monitor for 20m and decide.

eng-runtime: Splitter patch is up (11:27 UTC). Initial telemetry shows v3 traffic now steady at 5.1%. Throttles for legacy tenants down ~92% vs peak. Token-counter negative deltas still present in some aggregated metrics — need deeper trace.

Nora H.: I'll attach a quick query to list affected tenants and timespan:
```
SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as throttled_count
FROM request_events
WHERE deploy_tag='ratecap-v3' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-15T11:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-15T11:30:00Z' AND status_code IN (429,403)
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY throttled_count DESC
LIMIT 500;
```
Tom C.: Patch added unit test for splitter rounding and integration test for header parsing. I'll follow up with PR for token counter fix (use int64 and saturation logic).

ops-sre: PD escalation still open. Assigning owners: eng-runtime to root-cause & fix, infra to add traffic-splitter guard, ops to review flagging & rollout checklist, product/CS for customer messaging.

Ravi P.: Any estimate on customer credits? Billing will need a window and affected counts. CS, please coordinate.

CS Bot: CS-4799 created and initial outbound message drafted. Will wait for product approval.

eng-runtime: Proposed postmortem items: revert parity tests (ensure v2/v3 behavior matches), add fuzzing for header parse, strengthen canary guardrails (max-route-delta), and add counter-type checks to catch int overflow.

Nora H.: Monitoring: continue watching error rates and token deltas for 30 minutes. If stable we'll mark mitigated at 12:00 UTC.

ops-sre: Confirming mitigations held for 25 minutes. No further customer escalations since 11:40 UTC. Moving incident to post-incident review.

Ravi P.: Thanks team — quick summary: 1) Canary routing rounding + header parsing change caused exemptions to be ignored for legacy tenants; 2) token counter integer narrowing exacerbated enforcement; 3) mitigations: exclude legacy tenants, patch splitter rounding, plan token-counter fix; 4) follow-ups assigned. Postmortem meeting scheduled 15:00 UTC.
_notes: Incident thread for a ratecap canary routing/parsing regression: includes pager creation, quick mitigations (scope exclusion, splitter patch), rollback option, customer impact, and follow-ups for runtime fixes and tests.
